name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
summary: A unilateral horizontal pulling exercise that builds back strength and lat development while challenging core anti-rotation.

setup: Place your non-working knee and hand firmly on a flat bench to support your torso, or hinge at the hips with your non-working hand braced against a stable support.
Ensure your spine is neutral, chest proud, and hips squared to the floor.
Grip a dumbbell with your working hand using a neutral grip, letting the arm hang fully extended below your shoulder.
steps: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blade and driving your elbow backward toward your hip.
Pull the dumbbell smoothly until your upper arm is roughly parallel to your torso, keeping your elbow tucked close to your side.
Pause briefly at the top to contract your back muscles without twisting through your torso.
Lower the dumbbell in a controlled arc back to full extension, allowing the scapula to gently protract at the bottom.
instructions.breathing: Inhale at the bottom or as you lower the weight, and exhale forcefully as you row the dumbbell toward your hip.
cues: Pull through your elbow, not your hand.
Drive your elbow toward your pocket.
Keep your shoulders level and avoid twisting.

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso rotation to heave the weight up.
common_faults.correction: Keep your chest facing the floor throughout the movement; lighten the load if momentum is required.

common_faults.fault: Pulling the dumbbell up toward the chest or shoulder instead of the hip.
common_faults.correction: Row in a slight J-curve toward your hip to maximize lat engagement and avoid excessive upper-trap shrugging.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the range of motion short at the bottom.
common_faults.correction: Allow your arm and shoulder blade to reach full extension at the bottom for a thorough stretch of the lats.

precautions: Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding the lower back while supporting your weight.
